text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The newspaper editorial says Albanian President Sali Berisha was the initiator of the recent unrest among ethnic Albanians in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, in his last attempts to foment trouble before his resignation.

- The southern town of Berat, 120 km from Tirana, is in complete chaos with some 200 people killed and daily armed clashes between rival gangs. The state is making no effort to bring it under control.
- Some 200 Albanians returned from Italy last week after Italian authorities offered them half a million lira each.
- The army will help the Finance Ministry to collect customs duties at southern border posts.
- Ambassadors of the United States and the European Union in Tirana met the Socialist leader Fatos Nano to be briefed on his party's programme for government.

- The central election commission said Albanians had voted 66 percent for the republic and 33 percent for the monarchy but the monarchist Movement of Legality party does not recognise the result and will ask the Constitutional Court to rule on its legitimacy.

- The post-election government the Socialist party will make with the Social Democratic and the Democratic Alliance parties shows they will try to adopt the western type of governing, the editorial says.

- After a meeting with Prime Minister Bashkim Fino, President Sali Berisha said he would convene the new parliament when the central election commission gives the final results of the general election. Before resigning he will also nominate the new prime minister.
- Deputy Interior Minister Sokol Bare said police would start cracking down on crime and asked for the people's support.
- A European mission in Albania said the country has lost $900,000 a day during the recent unrest.

- The genocide trial against Ramiz Alia, the last communist president, is continously postponed as the court is waiting for the forming of the new Socialist government. -- Tirana newsroom +355 42 29825
